title: Slim bench scratchpad — Asha
content:
Slim bench quicksheet (purpose): lightweight nightly tracker for small prompt/quant/batch sweeps. Intent: capture quick signal, not full evaluation. Use for fast decision on whether to promote config to a proper run.

Table (CSV-ish):
run_id,date,prompt_variant,model,quant,batch_size,seq_len,p95_ms,mean_ms,cost_per_1k_tokens,score_notes
RB-2026-02A,2026-02-25,"short-instr-v1",gpt-redwood-compat-7B,int8,4,128,62,42,$0.85,"ok fluency, some truncation at end"
RB-2026-02B,2026-02-25,"short-instr-v2",gpt-redwood-compat-7B,int8,8,128,78,55,$0.72,"higher throughput, small drop in entailment on tests"
RB-2026-03C,2026-03-03,"open-ended-long",gpt-redwood-compat-13B,fp16,2,512,210,170,$2.60,"best quality but expensive; consider KV cache"
RB-2026-03D,2026-03-04,"open-ended-long",gpt-redwood-compat-13B,int8,2,512,245,198,$1.10,"int8 slower here (kernel mismatch) — investigate kernel selection"
RB-2026-03E,2026-03-08,"system-prompted",gpt-redwood-compat-7B,q4_0,6,256,95,71,$0.45,"good latency/cost balance; slight hallucination on numeric facts"

Quick observations (bullet-style):
- batch_size=8 on 7B int8 gives best cost/token but P95 increases non-linear when seq_len>256. probably batching policy mismatch.
- 13B fp16 dominates quality but cost 2.6x; int8 conversion currently slower -> maybe need different kernel/compilation flag.
- q4_0 is promising for mid-range seqs (128-256).

Ad-hoc micro-checks done:
- small prefix cache (enabled) reduced mean_ms by ~10% for repeated prompts (see RB-2026-02A -> RB-2026-02B diff).
- swapped to eager KV flush for 13B and saw mean_ms spike -> revert.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Why is int8 slower on 13B? check kernel table: aten vs custom-kernel mapping for 13B-int8 on ampere-1.
- Should I add a 7B q5-level try for long-form prompts? run quick sweep (q5, batch 4, seq_len 512).
- Add canary: when promoting config, include a 50-user synthetic traffic test (ramp 0->100 rps over 1m) to validate tail latency.

Small checklist before proper run: (x) fix prompt tokenization inconsistency; ( ) script to export p95 & cost per 1k tokens automatically; ( ) attach eval set (10 seeds)

Scratch math: cost calc quick formula used here:
- token_cost_est = (model_price_per_1k_tokens) * (tokens_out + tokens_in)/1000
- example: 7B int8 run RB-2026-02B: estimated tokens 320 per request -> cost ~0.72 (matches rough).

Links & anchors:
- Quick convo: #infra-bench in slack (see thread pinned Feb 26)
- PR with quant flags: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/78
- Larger notes: confluence:inference/batch-and-cache-notes

Next steps (short):
1) Re-run RB-2026-03D with kernel flag set to "prefer-optimized" and measure p95.
2) Add q5_0 sweep for 7B long form (small budget).
3) Draft a 1-paragraph proposal for team to add the 50-user canary to CI.

Fragmented thoughts (fast scribble):
- maybe we should auto-recommend batch sizes based on seq_len histogram — can re-use optimizer script from /bench tools.
- keep this sheet minimal; move canonical results to shared drive /engineering/applied-ml/benchmarks after validation.

-- end of sheet --
